ceiling_directive: Prove that a standard published varying-coefficient treatment-effect model with a constructible first-stage treatment learner is included in the proposed law–code experiment class, deriving the modifier-shift conditional-L1 certificate from stated primitive learner rates.
improvement_directive: Fully discharge the selected-contour Bahadur and multiplier result by proving the claimed uniform entropy, same-sample plug-in-score approximation, studentization, and fallback-probability rates rather than asserting them through grid-and-truncation summaries. Derive the admissible external-code certificate from a concrete learner under primitive conditions.
critique: The matched fixed-separation rate is established only for a newly constructed law–external-code class whose achievability theorem presumes a supplied code satisfying the bespoke conditional essential-supremum modifier-shift certificate; the note does not show that such a code can be learned or certified under a standard published HTE model. The all-band converse uses an exact-code Gaussian-regression subclass, so it validates the generic Hölder logarithmic rate over the larger class but does not establish that persistent code error or spectral separation creates the lower-bound difficulty. The load-bearing uniform Bahadur and multiplier lemma replaces several nontrivial steps—uniform entropy for the selected ratio-score class, dependence from same-sample plug-in scores, variance estimation, and sufficiently small failure probabilities—with abbreviated assertions rather than a complete derivation. The weak-separation section proves only an r_n lower bound and a constant-width upper bound, leaving the advertised spectral stability transition unresolved, although the framing correctly labels that part as open.
